sources.entry: PluXml - XML-based blog/CMS platform. (Source Code) GPL-3.0 PHP

summary.one_liner: PluXml is a flat-file PHP content management system for building lightweight websites and blogs without a database.
summary.what_it_does: PluXml stores its content in XML data files rather than a database. It provides a back-office for managing articles, static pages (which can contain PHP scripts), categories, tags, users, and comments. Archives can be browsed by month or by year, and a media manager handles uploaded files. Multiple users can be created with different grant levels, and the first user registered on a fresh install becomes the webmaster. The interface is translated into 11 languages, and themes and plugins can be added to customize the site. URL rewriting is supported when the server allows it.
use_cases: Run a personal or small business blog without a database
Host a simple flat-file CMS on basic PHP hosting
Manage blog articles, pages, and comments through a web back-office
Customize a site with themes and plugins
how_to_run: Download the latest release as a zip from GitHub and unzip it at the root of your site
Open the site in a browser and fill in the form to create the first user as webmaster
Access the back-office through the administration link at the bottom of the homepage
To update: back up the PluXml data folder, then unzip the latest release as for a fresh install
Connect to the site and accept the data upgrade prompt
stack: Apache2 mod_rewrite or NGinx (optional, for URL rewriting)
notable: No database: content is kept in XML data files
caveats: Supports PHP 5.6.34 through 8.1.2 only, so it may not run on newer PHP versions
URL rewriting needs Apache2 mod_rewrite or NGinx
Updates require backing up the data folder before upgrading
keywords: run a blog on shared hosting
